Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Acute severe unilateral (left-sided) headache awakening patient early AM; mild photophobia; no red-flag neurology/meningeal signs.  
- Most consistent with:  
  • Migraine without aura – favored by unilateral pain, photophobia, stress/sleep-deprivation trigger.  
  • Tension-type component possible given work-related stress and prior similar headaches.  
- Less likely but considered (DDx): cluster headache (lacks autonomic features); subarachnoid hemorrhage (very low suspicion but counselled on red-flags).  
- Management discussed: commence Ibuprofen (dose not documented) as first-line migraine therapy; may continue Paracetamol.  
- Non-pharmacologic: ensure 7–8 h sleep/night, hydrate ≥1.5–2 L water daily, consider one-week work break (self-certify), self-refer to local counselling service.  
- Safety-netting: provided written red-flag headache advice; instructed to re-contact if worsening or new symptoms.  
- Follow-up: telephone review in 1 week.
